title_en: The owned slave and the one given provision
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. A parable or similitude is not a dated event and is not placed in any order: the chapter states only what the ayat present as a similitude, what it is likened to, and what the ayat themselves say. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

chapters.title_en: The owned slave and the one given provision

claims.statement_en: God struck a similitude: a slave who is owned and has power over nothing, and one to whom God gave good provision from Himself, so that he spends from it in secret and openly; the ayah asks whether they are equal.
The ayah says that all praise is for God, but that most of them do not know.
God also struck a similitude of a pair of men, one of whom is dumb, has power over nothing and is a burden on his master, and brings no good wherever he sends him.
The ayah asks whether he is equal to one who commands justice and is on a straight path.

chapters.summary_md: God struck a similitude of a slave who is owned and has power over nothing, and of one given good provision who spends from it in secret and openly, and asks whether they are equal [c1]. He also struck a similitude of a man who is dumb and a burden on his master, and asks whether he is equal to one who commands justice [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md:
God struck a similitude: a slave who is owned and has power over nothing, and one to whom God gave good provision from Himself, so that he spends from it in secret and openly [c1]. The ayah asks whether they are equal [c1]. It says that all praise is for God, but that most of them do not know [c2].

God also struck a similitude of a pair of men [c3]. One of them is dumb, has power over nothing and is a burden on his master, and brings no good wherever he sends him [c3]. The ayah asks whether he is equal to one who commands justice and is on a straight path [c4].
chapters.deep_md: Each similitude is built as a contrast followed by a question: are they equal [c1][c4]. The first contrast is between having power over nothing and spending from good provision given by God [c1]. The next is between one who brings no good and one who commands justice and is on a straight path [c3][c4].
chapters.kids_md: God struck a similitude of a slave who is owned and has power over nothing, and of one given good provision who spends from it in secret and openly [c1]. The ayah asks whether they are equal [c1]. It says that all praise is for God [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the first similitude sets having power over nothing beside spending from provision that God gave [c1]. Another reading is that the later similitude sets one who brings no good beside one who commands justice and is on a straight path [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the men in these similitudes are; the ayat name no one and do not say whether the pictures are about particular persons.
- Not established: what the similitudes are about in the passage around them; the question are they equal is all the ayat state.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later sources link the pair of men to particular people; this draft does not repeat or vouch for them.
- The ayat themselves use the word for a similitude (mathal) in both places.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: none identified; a scholar should say whether any should be linked to these ayat.
The wording of abkam (dumb), kall (a burden) and of the straight path in 16:76 is for a scholar to confirm.
